meaning: at the moment/on the momentum of doing X, (unintentionally) Y happened

exercises.example_sentence: 立ち上がった拍子に、机に膝をぶつけてしまった。
exercises.translation: The moment I stood up, I banged my knee on the desk.
wrong_choice_explanations: ついでに means 'while at it', doing something deliberately on the occasion. 立ち上がったついでに膝をぶつけた makes banging the knee intentional, clashing with てしまった; 拍子に gives the accident of standing up.
あげく means 'after a long process, in the end (badly)'. 立ち上がったあげく needs a drawn-out struggle, but standing up is a single motion; 拍子に gives its instant, accidental result.
きり means 'did and then stayed that way'. 立ち上がったきり would mean the speaker never sat down again, which doesn't explain the bruised knee; 拍子に links standing up to the bump.
exercises.hiragana_full: たちあがったひょうしに、つくえにひざをぶつけてしまった。

末に means 'after a long process, finally'. くしゃみをした末に would need a long bout of sneezing, but one sneeze sent the glasses flying; 拍子に gives that instant.
きり means 'did and then stayed that way'. くしゃみをしたきり would mean the speaker sneezed and then did nothing more, unrelated to the glasses; 拍子に links the sneeze to them flying off.

あげく means 'after a long process, in the end (badly)'. 振り向いたあげく needs a drawn-out struggle, but turning round is a single motion; 拍子に gives its instant result.
ところに means 'just when…, (something arrived)'. 振り向いたところに needs something coming from outside, yet the collision was caused by the speaker's own turn; 拍子に gives that momentum.
